subject: CAIQ operational playbook + evidence showback request
messages:
From: Andrew Clarke <andrew.clarke@orchidbank.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: security@orchidbank.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ evidence request: operational playbook + runtime access showback

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking time during the vendor review. As part of OrchidBank's CAIQ review we need two things to close out a few operational controls:

1) An "operator playbook" (short runbook) that shows how your team collects and preserves runtime access logs for inference endpoints (what's collected, retention, redaction, how to produce a signed export).

2) A small evidence "showback": a sampling of runtime access logs (redacted) mapped to the relevant CAIQ control IDs (we only need ~48 hours worth of events) so our auditors can validate the collection and preservation steps.

Can you confirm scope and give an ETA for both items? If you prefer, a short call to walk through the format would help — our security lead (security@orchidbank.com) is on copy.

Thanks,
Andrew Clarke
Head of Vendor Security
OrchidBank

Attachments: orchid_caiq_matrix.xlsx (their current mapping template)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence request: operational playbook + runtime access showback

Marissa / Kim — looping you both in to own delivery.

Scope notes: OrchidBank wants the minimal reproducible artifacts auditors need: a concise operator playbook describing the extraction workflow, and a one-off redacted CSV sample showing the fields we collect (timestamp, request_id, model_id, user_id_hash, action, region, latency_ms, bytes_in/out). They included a template (attached).

Constraints / checklist for evidence:
- PII must be redacted (no raw prompt text) — use user_id_hash only.
- Logs must be signed (we can provide an affidavit and a GPG/signed manifest) OR provide a Drive link with an immutable export and hash.
- Provide mapping to CAIQ control IDs (list each control and point to the column/line in the CSV).
- Confirm retention window we demonstrate (they asked for 48 hours; we should confirm whether to pull a recent 48-hour window or a historical one).

Kim: can you run the extraction from the runtime log store and produce a redacted sample? Priyom: please prepare the operator_playbook-draft.md detailing the exact extraction commands and the signing/hash procedure; keep it concise (1-2 pages). Marissa: I'll coordinate the mapping and the final packaging to OrchidBank's template.

Target ETA: initial draft by tomorrow EOD PST (Mon 11/09), final package after their review 11/10 if they have small follow-ups. If anyone sees a blocker (PII, KMS/GCP/AWS access constraints), flag now.

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence request: operational playbook + runtime access showback

Quick status update:

- Extraction: kimberly ran a scoped query against the runtime telemetry index for a 48-hour window (2026-11-02 00:00 UTC -> 2026-11-04 00:00 UTC) and exported a redacted CSV sample. Attached: runtime_access_log_sample.csv (user_id -> hashed, prompts removed).
- Playbook: Priyom attached operator_playbook-draft.md with step-by-step commands using our internal tooling (log-export CLI and signed-manifest.sh). It includes the KMS key id used for signing and an example manifest hash.
- Mapping: I've started the CAIQ crosswalk in Orchid's template; mapping rows are commented where we rely on runtime KV caching and batching to meet evidence expectations.

Open questions for OrchidBank:
1) Retention window: they asked for 48 hours; we pulled a 48-hour sample but can do a recent window if they prefer.
2) Signing: we used an internal HSM-backed signing flow and included the manifest hash; do they want a notarized affidavit instead?

Attachments: runtime_access_log_sample.csv (redacted), operator_playbook-draft.md (draft).

If no blockers, I'll package and send to Andrew/security by EOD with a short note explaining redactions and how to verify the manifest.

—Marissa
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Andrew Clarke <andrew.clarke@orchidbank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@orchidbank.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence request: operational playbook + runtime access showback

Marissa — this is perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of small asks before we close: 

1) Can you confirm which CAIQ control IDs the runtime_access_log_sample.csv demonstrates? A short bullet list in the message body is fine (e.g., CCM-ACCESS-01 -> column X / example row).
2) For the signing: the auditors prefer a signed manifest plus the public key fingerprint in the playbook. If you can add the fingerprint to operator_playbook-draft.md that should suffice.

Once we have those two items we'll slot this into our CAIQ package and expect no further questions. Appreciate the concise playbook.

Regards,
Andrew
Head of Vendor Security, OrchidBank
